NASB.1: Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where [the LORD] had appeared to his father David, at the place that David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
NASB.2: He began to build on the second [day] in the second month of the fourth year of his reign.
NASB.3: Now these are the foundations which Solomon laid for building the house of God. The length in cubits, according to the old standard [was] sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
NASB.4: The porch which was in front of the house was as long as the width of the house, twenty cubits, and the height 120; and inside he overlaid it with pure gold.
NASB.5: He overlaid the main room with cypress wood and overlaid it with fine gold, and ornamented it with palm trees and chains.
NASB.6: Further, he adorned the house with precious stones; and the gold was gold from Parvaim.
NASB.7: He also overlaid the house with gold-- the beams, the thresholds and its walls and its doors; and he carved cherubim on the walls.
NASB.8: Now he made the room of the holy of holies: its length across the width of the house [was] twenty cubits, and its width [was] twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with fine gold, [amounting] to 600 talents.
NASB.9: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He also overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
NASB.10: Then he made two sculptured cherubim in the room of the holy of holies and overlaid them with gold.
NASB.11: The wingspan of the cherubim [was] twenty cubits; the wing of one, of five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and [its] other wing, of five cubits, touched the wing of the other cherub.
NASB.12: The wing of the other cherub, of five cubits, touched the wall of the house; and [its] other wing of five cubits was attached to the wing of the first cherub.
NASB.13: The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits, and they stood on their feet facing the [main] room.
NASB.14: He made the veil of violet, purple, crimson and fine linen, and he worked cherubim on it.
NASB.15: He also made two pillars for the front of the house, thirty-five cubits high, and the capital on the top of each [was] five cubits.
NASB.16: He made chains in the inner sanctuary and placed [them] on the tops of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates and placed [them] on the chains.
NASB.17: He erected the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and the other on the left, and named the one on the right Jachin and the one on the left Boaz.

ESV.1: Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD  had appeared to David his father, at the place that David had appointed, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
ESV.2: He began to build in the second month of the fourth year of his reign.
ESV.3: These are Solomon's measurements  for building the house of God: the length, in cubits  of the old standard, was sixty cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits.
ESV.4: The vestibule in front of the nave of the house was twenty cubits long, equal to the width of the house,  and its height was 120 cubits. He overlaid it on the inside with pure gold.
ESV.5: The nave he lined with cypress and covered it with fine gold and made palms and chains on it.
ESV.6: He adorned the house with settings of precious stones. The gold was gold of Parvaim.
ESV.7: So he lined the house with gold — its beams, its thresholds, its walls, and its doors — and he carved cherubim on the walls.
ESV.8: And he made the Most Holy Place. Its length, corresponding to the breadth of the house, was twenty cubits, and its breadth was twenty cubits. He overlaid it with 600 talents  of fine gold.
ESV.9: The weight of gold for the nails was fifty shekels.  And he overlaid the upper chambers with gold.
ESV.10: In the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of wood  and overlaid  them with gold.
ESV.11: The wings of the cherubim together extended twenty cubits: one wing of the one, of five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, of five cubits, touched the wing of the other cherub;
ESV.12: and of this cherub, one wing, of five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and the other wing, also of five cubits, was joined to the wing of the first cherub.
ESV.13: The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits. The cherubim  stood on their feet, facing the nave.
ESV.14: And he made the veil of blue and purple and crimson fabrics and fine linen, and he worked cherubim on it.
ESV.15: In front of the house he made two pillars thirty-five cubits high, with a capital of five cubits on the top of each.
ESV.16: He made chains like a necklace  and put them on the tops of the pillars, and he made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.
ESV.17: He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the south, the other on the north; that on the south he called Jachin, and that on the north Boaz.

NKJV.1: Now Solomon began to build the house of the LORD at Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David, at the place that David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

NKJV.3: This is the foundation which Solomon laid for building the house of God: The length was sixty cubits (by cubits according to the former measure) and the width twenty cubits.
NKJV.4: And the vestibule that was in front of the sanctuary was twenty cubits long across the width of the house, and the height was one hundred and twenty. He overlaid the inside with pure gold.
NKJV.5: The larger room he paneled with cypress which he overlaid with fine gold, and he carved palm trees and chainwork on it.
NKJV.6: And he decorated the house with precious stones for beauty, and the gold was gold from Parvaim.
NKJV.7: He also overlaid the house—the beams and doorposts, its walls and doors—with gold; and he carved cherubim on the walls.
NKJV.8: And he made the Most Holy Place. Its length was according to the width of the house, twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits. He overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.
NKJV.9: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold; and he overlaid the upper area with gold.
NKJV.10: In the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim, fashioned by carving, and overlaid them with gold.
NKJV.11: The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits in overall length: one wing of the one cherub was five cubits, touching the wall of the room, and the other wing was five cubits, touching the wing of the other cherub;
NKJV.12: one wing of the other cherub was five cubits, touching the wall of the room, and the other wing also was five cubits, touching the wing of the other cherub.
NKJV.13: The wings of these cherubim spanned twenty cubits overall. They stood on their feet, and they faced inward.
NKJV.14: And he made the veil of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and wove cherubim into it.
NKJV.15: Also he made in front of the temple two pillars thirty-five cubits high, and the capital that was on the top of each of them was five cubits.
NKJV.16: He made wreaths of chainwork, as in the inner sanctuary, and put them on top of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates, and put them on the wreaths of chainwork.
NKJV.17: Then he set up the pillars before the temple, one on the right hand and the other on the left; he called the name of the one on the right hand Jachin, and the name of the one on the left Boaz.

NLT.1: So Solomon began to build the Temple of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to David, his father. The Temple was built on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite, the site that David had selected.
NLT.2: The construction began in midspring, during the fourth year of Solomon’s reign.
NLT.3: These are the dimensions Solomon used for the foundation of the Temple of God (using the old standard of measurement). It was 90 feet long and 30 feet wide.
NLT.4: The entry room at the front of the Temple was 30 feet wide, running across the entire width of the Temple, and 30 feet high. He overlaid the inside with pure gold.
NLT.5: He paneled the main room of the Temple with cypress wood, overlaid it with fine gold, and decorated it with carvings of palm trees and chains.
NLT.6: He decorated the walls of the Temple with beautiful jewels and with gold from the land of Parvaim.
NLT.7: He overlaid the beams, thresholds, walls, and doors throughout the Temple with gold, and he carved figures of cherubim on the walls.
NLT.8: He made the Most Holy Place 30 feet wide, corresponding to the width of the Temple, and 30 feet deep. He overlaid its interior with 23 tons of fine gold.
NLT.9: The gold nails that were used weighed 20 ounces each. He also overlaid the walls of the upper rooms with gold.
NLT.10: He made two figures shaped like cherubim, overlaid them with gold, and placed them in the Most Holy Place.
NLT.11: The total wingspan of the two cherubim standing side by side was 30 feet. One wing of the first figure was 7 1⁄2 feet long, and it touched the Temple wall. The other wing, also 7 1⁄2 feet long, touched one of the wings of the second figure.
NLT.12: In the same way, the second figure had one wing 7 1⁄2 feet long that touched the opposite wall. The other wing, also 7 1⁄2 feet long, touched the wing of the first figure.
NLT.13: So the wingspan of the two cherubim side by side was 30 feet. They stood on their feet and faced out toward the main room of the Temple.
NLT.14: Across the entrance of the Most Holy Place he hung a curtain made of fine linen, decorated with blue, purple, and scarlet thread and embroidered with figures of cherubim.
NLT.15: For the front of the Temple, he made two pillars that were 27 feet tall, each topped by a capital extending upward another 7 1⁄2 feet.
NLT.16: He made a network of interwoven chains and used them to decorate the tops of the pillars. He also made 100 decorative pomegranates and attached them to the chains.
NLT.17: Then he set up the two pillars at the entrance of the Temple, one to the south of the entrance and the other to the north. He named the one on the south Jakin, and the one on the north Boaz.

WEB.1: Then Solomon began to build Yahweh’s house at Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where Yahweh appeared to David his father, which he prepared in the place that David had appointed, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
WEB.2: He began to build in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
WEB.3: Now these are the foundations which Solomon laid for the building of God’s house. The length by cubits  after the first measure was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
WEB.4: The porch that was in front, its length, according to the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and the height one hundred twenty; and he overlaid it within with pure gold.
WEB.5: He made the larger room with a ceiling of cypress wood, which he overlaid with fine gold, and ornamented it with palm trees and chains.
WEB.6: He decorated the house with precious stones for beauty. The gold was gold from Parvaim.
WEB.7: He also overlaid the house, the beams, the thresholds, its walls, and its doors with gold; and engraved cherubim on the walls.
WEB.8: He made the most holy place. Its length, according to the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents.
WEB.9: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels  of gold. He overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
WEB.10: In the most holy place he made two cherubim by carving; and they overlaid them with gold.
WEB.11: The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long: the wing of the one was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house; and the other wing was five cubits, reaching to the wing of the other cherub.
WEB.12: The wing of the other cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house; and the other wing was five cubits, joining to the wing of the other cherub.
WEB.13: The wings of these cherubim spread themselves out twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.
WEB.14: He made the veil of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and ornamented it with cherubim.
WEB.15: Also he made before the house two pillars of thirty-five cubits height, and the capital that was on the top of each of them was five cubits.
WEB.16: He made chains in the inner sanctuary, and put them on the tops of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates, and put them on the chains.
WEB.17: He set up the pillars before the temple, one on the right hand, and the other on the left; and called the name of that on the right hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz.

CSB17.1: Then Solomon began <sup>ⓕ</sup> to build the LORD’s temple in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah <sup>ⓖ</sup> where the LORD <sup>[1]</sup> had appeared to his father David, at the site David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan <sup>[2]</sup> the Jebusite.
CSB17.2: He began to build on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.
CSB17.3: These are Solomon’s foundations <sup>[3]</sup> for building God’s temple: the length <sup>[4]</sup> was ninety feet, <sup>[5]</sup> and the width thirty feet. <sup>[6]</sup>
CSB17.4: The portico, which was across the front extending across the width of the temple, was thirty feet wide; its height was thirty feet; <sup>[7]</sup> he overlaid its inner surface with pure gold.
CSB17.5: The larger room <sup>[8]</sup> he paneled with cypress wood, overlaid with fine gold, and decorated with palm trees and chains.
CSB17.6: He adorned the temple with precious stones for beauty, and the gold was the gold of Parvaim.
CSB17.7: He overlaid the temple — the beams, the thresholds, its walls and doors — with gold, <sup>ⓗ</sup> and he carved cherubim on the walls. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.8: Then he made the most holy place; its length corresponded to the width of the temple, 30 feet, and its width was 30 feet. <sup>ⓙ</sup> He overlaid it with forty-five thousand pounds <sup>[9]</sup> of fine gold.
CSB17.9: The weight of the nails was twenty ounces <sup>[10]</sup> of gold, and he overlaid the ceiling with gold.
CSB17.10: He made <sup>ⓚ</sup> two cherubim of sculptured work, for the most holy place, and he overlaid them with gold.
CSB17.11: The overall length of the wings of the cherubim was 30 feet: the wing of one was 7½ feet, <sup>[11]</sup> touching the wall of the room; its other wing was 7½ feet, touching the wing of the other cherub.
CSB17.12: The wing of the other <sup>[12]</sup> cherub was 7½ feet, touching the wall of the room; its other wing was 7½ feet, reaching the wing of the other cherub.
CSB17.13: The wingspan of these cherubim was 30 feet. They stood on their feet and faced the larger room. <sup>[13]</sup>
CSB17.14: He made the curtain of blue, purple, and crimson yarn and fine linen, and he wove cherubim into it. <sup>ⓛ</sup>

CSB17.16: He had made chainwork in the inner sanctuary and also put it on top of the pillars. <sup>ⓝ</sup> He made a hundred pomegranates and fastened them into the chainwork.
CSB17.17: Then he set up the pillars in front of the sanctuary, one on the right and one on the left. He named the one on the right Jachin <sup>[15]</sup> and the one on the left Boaz. <sup>[16]</sup>

AMP.1: Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared to his father David, in the place that David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
AMP.2: Solomon began to build on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.
AMP.3: Now this is the [measurement of the] foundation which Solomon laid for the house of God: the length in cubits—by the old standard of measure—was sixty cubits (90 ft.), and the width was twenty cubits (30 ft.).
AMP.4: The porch in front of the house was as long as the width of the house, twenty cubits, and the height was 120 cubits. He overlaid it inside with pure gold.
AMP.5: He overlaid the main room [the Holy Place] with cypress wood and overlaid it with fine gold, and decorated it with palm trees and chains.
AMP.6: And he adorned the house with precious stones; and the gold was gold from Parvaim.
AMP.7: He also overlaid the house [the Holy Place] with gold—the beams, the thresholds, and its walls and its doors; and he carved cherubim on the walls.
AMP.8: Now he made the room of the Holy of Holies: its length equaling the width of the house was twenty cubits, and its width was twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with 600 talents of fine gold.
AMP.9: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He also overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
AMP.10: And in the Holy of Holies he made two sculptured cherubim, and overlaid them with gold.
AMP.11: The wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits: one wing of one cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house, and its other wing, of five cubits, touched the other cherub's wing.
AMP.12: The wing of the other cherub, of five cubits, touched the wall of the house; and its other wing of five cubits touched the wing of the first cherub.
AMP.13: The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits. The cherubim stood on their feet, their faces toward the Holy Place (the main room).
AMP.14: He made the veil [between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies] of blue, purple, and crimson colors, and fine linen, and embroidered cherubim on it.
AMP.15: He also made two pillars for the front of the house, thirty-five cubits high, and the capital on the top of each one was five cubits.
AMP.16: He made chains [like a necklace] in the inner sanctuary and put them on the tops of the pillars; and he made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.
AMP.17: He erected the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right, the other on the left, and named the one on the right Jachin (may He establish) and the one on the left Boaz (in Him is strength).

NIV.1:
Solomon Builds the Temple
Then Solomon began to build the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the Lord had appeared to his father David. It was on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite, the place provided by David.
NIV.2: He began building on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.
NIV.3: The foundation Solomon laid for building the temple of God was sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide (using the cubit of the old standard).
NIV.4:
The portico at the front of the temple was twenty cubits long across the width of the building and twenty cubits high.
He overlaid the inside with pure gold.
NIV.5: He paneled the main hall with pine and covered it with fine gold and decorated it with palm tree and chain designs.
NIV.6: He adorned the temple with precious stones. And the gold he used was gold of Parvaim.
NIV.7: He overlaid the ceiling beams, doorframes, walls and doors of the temple with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
NIV.8: He built the Most Holy Place, its length corresponding to the width of the temple—twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. He overlaid the inside with six hundred talents of fine gold.
NIV.9: The gold nails weighed fifty shekels. He also overlaid the upper parts with gold.
NIV.10: In the Most Holy Place he made a pair of sculptured cherubim and overlaid them with gold.
NIV.11: The total wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long and touched the temple wall, while its other wing, also five cubits long, touched the wing of the other cherub.
NIV.12: Similarly one wing of the second cherub was five cubits long and touched the other temple wall, and its other wing, also five cubits long, touched the wing of the first cherub.
NIV.13: The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing the main hall.
NIV.14: He made the curtain of blue, purple and crimson yarn and fine linen, with cherubim worked into it.
NIV.15: In the front of the temple he made two pillars, which together were thirty-five cubits long, each with a capital on top measuring five cubits.
NIV.16: He made interwoven chains and put them on top of the pillars. He also made a hundred pomegranates and attached them to the chains.
NIV.17: He erected the pillars in the front of the temple, one to the south and one to the north. The one to the south he named Jakin and the one to the north Boaz.

MSG.1: So Solomon broke ground, launched construction of the house of God in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, the place where God had appeared to his father David. The precise site, the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite, had been designated by David.
MSG.2: He broke ground on the second day in the second month of the fourth year of his rule.
MSG.3: These are the dimensions that Solomon set for the construction of the house of God: ninety feet long and thirty feet wide.
MSG.4:
The porch in front stretched the width of the building, that is, thirty feet; and it was thirty feet high.
The interior was gold-plated.
MSG.5: He paneled the main hall with cypress and veneered it with fine gold engraved with palm tree and chain designs.
MSG.6: He decorated the building with precious stones and gold from Parvaim.
MSG.7: Everything was coated with gold veneer: rafters, doorframes, walls, and doors. Cherubim were engraved on the walls.
MSG.8: He made the Holy of Holies a cube, thirty feet wide, long, and high. It was veneered with 600 talents (something over twenty-two tons) of gold.
MSG.9: The gold nails weighed fifty shekels (a little over a pound). The upper rooms were also veneered in gold.
MSG.10: He made two sculptures of cherubim, gigantic angel-like figures, for the Holy of Holies, both veneered with gold.
MSG.11: The combined wingspread of the side-by-side cherubim (each wing measuring seven and a half feet) stretched from wall to wall, thirty feet.
MSG.13: They stood erect facing the main hall.
MSG.14: He fashioned the curtain of violet, purple, and crimson fabric and worked a cherub design into it.
MSG.15: He made two huge free-standing pillars, each fifty-two feet tall, their capitals extending another seven and a half feet.
MSG.16: The top of each pillar was set off with an elaborate filigree of chains, like necklaces, from which hung a hundred pomegranates.
MSG.17: He placed the pillars in front of The Temple, one on the right, and the other on the left. The right pillar he named Jakin (Security) and the left pillar he named Boaz (Stability).

NRSVCE.1: Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David, at the place that David had designated, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
NRSVCE.2: He began to build on the second day of the second month of the fourth year of his reign.
NRSVCE.3: These are Solomon’s measurements for building the house of God: the length, in cubits of the old standard, was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
NRSVCE.4: The vestibule in front of the nave of the house was twenty cubits long, across the width of the house; and its height was one hundred twenty cubits. He overlaid it on the inside with pure gold.
NRSVCE.5: The nave he lined with cypress, covered it with fine gold, and made palms and chains on it.
NRSVCE.6: He adorned the house with settings of precious stones. The gold was gold from Parvaim.
NRSVCE.7: So he lined the house with gold — its beams, its thresholds, its walls, and its doors; and he carved cherubim on the walls.
NRSVCE.8: He made the most holy place; its length, corresponding to the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and its width was twenty cubits; he overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.
NRSVCE.9: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper chambers with gold.
NRSVCE.10: In the most holy place he made two carved cherubim and overlaid them with gold.
NRSVCE.11: The wings of the cherubim together extended twenty cubits: one wing of the one, five cubits long, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits long, touched the wing of the other cherub;
NRSVCE.12: and of this cherub, one wing, five cubits long, touched the wall of the house, and the other wing, also five cubits long, was joined to the wing of the first cherub.
NRSVCE.13: The wings of these cherubim extended twenty cubits; the cherubim stood on their feet, facing the nave.
NRSVCE.14: And Solomon made the curtain of blue and purple and crimson fabrics and fine linen, and worked cherubim into it.
NRSVCE.15: In front of the house he made two pillars thirty-five cubits high, with a capital of five cubits on the top of each.
NRSVCE.16: He made encircling chains and put them on the tops of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates, and put them on the chains.
NRSVCE.17: He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right, the other on the left; the one on the right he called Jachin, and the one on the left, Boaz.

NET.1: Solomon began building the LORD’s temple in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David. This was the place that David prepared at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
NET.2: He began building on the second day of the second month of the fourth year of his reign.
NET.3: Solomon laid the foundation for God’s temple; its length (determined according to the old standard of measure) was 90 feet, and its width 30 feet.
NET.4: The porch in front of the main hall was 30 feet long, corresponding to the width of the temple, and its height was 30 feet. He plated the inside with pure gold.
NET.5: He paneled the main hall with boards made from evergreen trees and plated it with fine gold, decorated with palm trees and chains.
NET.6: He decorated the temple with precious stones; the gold he used came from Parvaim.
NET.7: He overlaid the temple’s rafters, thresholds, walls and doors with gold; he carved decorative cherubim on the walls.
NET.8: He made the most holy place; its length was 30 feet, corresponding to the width of the temple, and its width 30 feet. He plated it with 600 talents of fine gold.
NET.9: The gold nails weighed 50 shekels; he also plated the upper areas with gold.
NET.10: In the most holy place he made two images of cherubim and plated them with gold.
NET.11: The combined wing span of the cherubs was 30 feet. One of the first cherub’s wings was seven and one-half feet long and touched one wall of the temple; its other wing was also seven and one-half feet long and touched one of the second cherub’s wings.
NET.12: Likewise one of the second cherub’s wings was seven and one-half feet long and touched the other wall of the temple; its other wing was also seven and one-half feet long and touched one of the first cherub’s wings.
NET.13: The combined wingspan of these cherubim was 30 feet. They stood upright, facing inward.
NET.14: He made the curtain out of violet, purple, crimson, and white fabrics, and embroidered on it decorative cherubim.
NET.15: In front of the temple he made two pillars which had a combined length of 52Â½ feet, with each having a plated capital seven and one-half feet high.
NET.16: He made ornamental chains and put them on top of the pillars. He also made one hundred pomegranate-shaped ornaments and arranged them within the chains.
NET.17: He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right side and the other on the left. He named the one on the right Jachin, and the one on the left Boaz.
